inputs.name: LTEE regime
inputs.value: 12 populations, each transferred daily at 1:100, evolved independently
inputs.cite: Q312 (Z23003785 s1); branch-E E q1 (Z23020792); parameters ltee.generations_per_day; E9; Day s5.2

day.reading: gene flow only redistributes alleles; in a structured species a species-wide substitution waits on migrants (an extra stage, slower fixation), and between lineages gene flow erases differences, so it cannot help close the accounting gap
day.holds: gene flow creates and fixes no allele, so it adds no substitutions to the count; between lineages it works against divergence (direction agreed; K4: low materiality); if structure lengthens transit, an empty-start count loses more (M-201); the LTEE flasks have no gene flow, so its G_f carries no such stage

critic.reading: pace is a rate over a window (M-115); structure changes latency, not the neutral rate
critic.holds: Day's own Hard Limits paper states Maruyama invariance: under conservative migration the neutral rate is exactly mu (M-209: k/mu = 1), so structure does not slow neutral substitution as a rate; the post gives no transit time and none is held for selected alleles; the LTEE comparison turns on transfer (M-103, M-006), not on gene flow

notes: Model choice, qualitative. Both readings of 'pace' are recorded; no structured-population transit time is derived (brief: not in scope) and none is held, so the latency claim is quoted, not tested. Selected-case fixation times in subdivided populations would need Z18167588's Whitlock & Barton passage or a primary source; neither is quoted in held files.
